benefits.en: The telephone rang in the dead of night.
benefits.zh: 你可以用一個簡潔的固定表達，代替「在夜晚最黑暗、最深沉和最寂靜的時候」這段較長的解釋。

benefits.en: The expression immediately suggests darkness, silence and sleeping people.
benefits.zh: 這個表達能立即令人聯想到黑暗、寂靜，以及大部分人已經熟睡的畫面。

benefits.titleEn: It Makes Unexpected Events More Striking
benefits.titleZh: 突出事件的突然或異常
benefits.en: The second sentence makes the event sound more unusual and unsettling.
benefits.zh: 第二句更能突出事件發生得非常突然，而且可能令人感到不安。

benefits.en: The expression can quickly establish when an event happened and what the surroundings felt like.
benefits.zh: 這個表達可以同時交代事件發生的時間及當時的環境氣氛。

benefits.en: In the dead of night, the alarm rang. However, the idiom is not automatically better than a plain time expression. Use it only when its vivid nighttime atmosphere suits the message.
benefits.zh: 這個時間短語可以放在句末，也可以放在句首，令句式更加靈活。 不過，慣用語並非在任何情況下都比普通時間表達更好。 只有當深夜氣氛對句子有實際作用時， 才應使用。

origin.statusEn: Exact Origin Unknown; Early Written Use Documented
origin.statusZh: 確切來源不明；已有早期書面記錄

history.en: An early recorded related form, in the dead of the night, appears in Edward Hall’s Chronicle of 1548. This is an early surviving written record, not proof that Hall invented the expression. Shakespeare later used the shorter wording in Twelfth Night: “even in the dead of night”.
history.zh: 一個有早期記錄的相關形式 in the dead of the night，出現在 Edward Hall 於1548年出版的《編年史》中。 這只是目前可找到的早期書面記錄，並不能證明 Hall 創造了這個表達。 莎士比亞後來亦在《第十二夜》中使用了較短的形式 in the dead of night。

history.en: The idea of the night reaching its deepest point naturally developed into a fixed description of the very late hours when most people are asleep and the surroundings are dark and quiet.
history.zh: 夜晚到達最深沉的時刻這個概念，逐漸演變成一個固定表達，用來描述大部分人已入睡、周圍黑暗而寂靜的深夜時段。

origin.memoryEn: Imagine the night at its deepest point: almost no light, little sound and most people asleep.
origin.memoryZh: 想像夜晚最深沉的一刻：幾乎沒有光線、四周寂靜，大部分人都已入睡。

rules.en: The dog barked at the dead of night.
rules.zh: 一般應使用介詞 in，組成完整時間短語 in the dead of night。

rules.titleZh: 冠詞 the 是固定部分，不可省略
rules.zh: 冠詞 the 是固定部分，不可省略。

rules.titleEn: “Dead” Does Not Mean That Someone Has Died
rules.en: In this expression, dead helps describe the night at its deepest, darkest or quietest point. Do not translate the expression literally as: Natural Chinese meanings include:
rules.zh: 這裏的 dead 並不是指有人死亡，而是強調夜晚最深沉、最黑暗或最寂靜的時段。 死亡的夜晚深夜時分； 夜深人靜時； 萬籟俱寂之時； 夜晚最深沉的時候。

rules.titleEn: It Does Not Necessarily Mean Exactly Midnight
rules.en: The expression refers to a general part of the night, not one exact clock time.
rules.zh: 這個表達並不一定指正好午夜十二時，而是泛指夜晚最深、最黑暗或最寂靜的時段。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for the Early Evening
rules.en: We had dinner at eight in the evening.
rules.zh: 一般情況下，晚上八時並不算 the dead of night。

rules.en: Unless the unusual time is important, the vivid idiom may add nothing useful.
rules.zh: 只有當「深夜發生」對事件的氣氛、驚訝程度或重要性有明顯作用時，才應使用這個表達。

rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a possibility into a completed fact.
rules.zh: 原句表示可能性時，答案也必須保留相同的可能程度，不可擅自改成已經發生的事實。

rules.titleEn: Use a Comma After an Initial Phrase
rules.en: In the dead of night the alarm began to ring.
rules.zh: 當 In the dead of night 放在句首時，後面應使用逗號。
